# Agent Instructions

## Pre-Commit: Documentation Check

Before committing changes, verify documentation is updated to reflect code changes:

1. **README.md** - Update if changes affect:
   - Plugin usage (`/devcontainer`, `/worktree`, `/workspaces` commands)
   - Configuration options (`~/.config/opencode/devcontainers/config.json`)
   - Installation steps or dependencies
   - Usage examples

2. **CONTRIBUTING.md** - Update if changes affect:
   - Development setup or workflow
   - Test commands or patterns
   - Release process
   - Project structure

3. **plugin/command/\*.md** - Update if changes affect:
   - Command arguments or behavior
   - Examples

## Post-PR: Release and Upgrade Workflow

Releases are event-driven, never push-driven: merging to main never
publishes anything. To cut a release:

1. Ensure `main` is green
2. `gh release create vX.Y.Z --target main --generate-notes` (the Releases
   UI works the same — publishing the release is what triggers the pipeline)
3. The `Publish release` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` triggers on the
   release event and:
   1. stamps the tag's version into the checkout (`package.json` commits a
      placeholder; the release tag is the source of truth)
   2. publishes the canonical version to npmjs (`registry.npmjs.org`), with
      provenance
   3. mirrors that version to the GitHub Packages npm registry
      (`npm.pkg.github.com`) via `scripts/publish-github-packages.mjs`
4. Re-running the publish job is safe: both publishes skip when the version
   is already present. Draft/prerelease releases are ignored by the job;
   promoting a prerelease to a stable release does publish (GitHub emits
   the `released` event for that transition). A release whose version is
   lower than the current `latest` is refused — backports are published
   manually with an explicit dist-tag. A stable release fires both the
   `published` and `released` events, so the publish job runs twice per
   release: the first run publishes; the second skips every step whose
   version it finds already present — and when it catches npm's staging
   window (`npm view` still 404 for the just-published version), it
   attempts the duplicate publish, treats the registry's version conflict
   as success, and continues to the mirror, which skips or tolerates its
   duplicate the same way. If several releases are cut in quick
   succession, GitHub keeps only one queued publish run — a superseded run
   can be re-run from the Actions tab (both publishes are idempotent, so
   re-runs never duplicate).

The npmjs publish uses **trusted publishing (OIDC)** — no npm token secret
exists in the repo. `id-token: write` lets the npm CLI exchange a
short-lived OIDC token for publish credentials; npm validates it against
the trusted publisher configured on npmjs.com. The GitHub Packages mirror
uses the job's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`packages: write`), also no secret.

Trusted publisher (configured once on npmjs.com → the package → Settings →
Trusted publishing → GitHub Actions, or via `npm trust github`):

| Field                | Value                                         |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Organization or user | `timlaing`                                    |
| Repository           | `opencode-devcontainers`                      |
| Workflow filename    | `ci.yml`                                      |
| Environment name     | _(leave blank — the job sets no environment)_ |

Two gotchas: the workflow filename must match exactly (`ci.yml`, not the
full path), and a trusted-publisher config must complete its **first
publish within 2 days** of being created or it expires and must be
re-created. Trusted publishing also cannot create a package's first-ever
version unless the pending/first config is in place — so create the config
_before_ the first release, not after.

### Verify Release

```bash
gh release list -R timlaing/opencode-devcontainers -L 1
npm view @timlaing/opencode-devcontainers version   # npmjs (canonical)
npm view @timlaing/opencode-devcontainers version --registry https://npm.pkg.github.com
```

The npmjs lookup needs no token (public reads are open). GitHub Packages
requires authentication even for reads of public packages; add
`//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=$NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` to `~/.npmrc` and
export a token with `read:packages`, or that `npm view` call fails.

### Upgrade

OpenCode automatically updates npm plugins on startup. Just restart OpenCode.

To force a specific version:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers@1.0.0"]
}
```

### Config Locations

- Main config: `~/.config/opencode/devcontainers/config.json`
- Cache/state: `~/.cache/opencode-devcontainers/`
- Clones: `~/.local/share/opencode/clone/`
- Worktrees: `~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/`

If config format changed, check release notes:

```bash
gh release view -R timlaing/opencode-devcontainers
```

## Repository automation

- `main` runs CI (`Plugin tests` + `Release`), the `npm dependency vulnerabilities` audit, and the SonarQube quality gate. The SonarQube workflow fails if the `SONAR_TOKEN` secret is missing.
- Issue forms set `bug`/`enhancement` plus `needs-triage`; the `Automatic labels` workflow adds a component label from the bug form and path/conventional title labels on PRs. Labels are defined in the repository's Labels settings.
- A stale workflow marks quiet issues after 60 days and PRs after 30; the labels `keep-open`, `security` and `priority: high` are exempt.

OpenCode plugin for isolated branch workspaces using devcontainers (OpenCode V1
also supports git worktrees).

**Full documentation: [timlaing.github.io/opencode-devcontainers](https://timlaing.github.io/opencode-devcontainers/)**

> **Note**: This is a community project and is not built by or affiliated with the OpenCode team.

## OpenCode V2 support

This fork supports both OpenCode plugin APIs from one package:

| OpenCode     | Config                                            | Devcontainers | Worktrees         |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ----------------- |
| V2 (2.x)     | `"plugins": ["@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"]` | ✅            | Native V2 support |
| V1 ≥ 1.18.29 | `"plugin": ["@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"]`  | ✅            | ✅ `/worktree`    |
| V1 < 1.18.29 | `"plugin": ["opencode-devcontainers@0.5.1"]`      | ✅            | ✅                |

See [Migrating to OpenCode V2](https://timlaing.github.io/opencode-devcontainers/migration/) for details.

## Why?

When working on multiple branches, you need isolated development environments:

- **Devcontainers** provide full container isolation (different dependencies, databases, etc.)
- **Worktrees** provide lightweight filesystem isolation (same dependencies, just different code)

This plugin provides both options with:

- Session state management (the agent remembers your workspace)
- Auto-assigned ports from a configurable range (13000-13099)
- Automatic copying of gitignored secrets (.env, credentials, etc.)
- Unified workspace management and cleanup

## Installation

Add to your `opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc
// OpenCode V2
{
  "plugins": ["@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"],
}
```

```jsonc
// OpenCode V1 (>= 1.18.29)
{
  "plugin": ["@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"],
}
```

OpenCode automatically installs npm plugins on startup. The package is
published to both [npmjs](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers)
(recommended — public reads need no token) and
[GitHub Packages](https://github.com/timlaing/opencode-devcontainers/packages).
Because both use the `@timlaing` scope, your npm/bun config must map that
scope to one of them — e.g. `@timlaing:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org`
for npmjs. Full instructions (including the git-based install and the
V1 < 1.18.29 pin) are in the
[installation guide](https://timlaing.github.io/opencode-devcontainers/installation/).

### Dependencies

- For devcontainers: `devcontainer` CLI - Install with: `npm install -g @devcontainers/cli`
- For worktrees: Just git (no additional dependencies)

## Usage

### Devcontainers (Full Container Isolation)

```
/devcontainer feature-x    # Start/target a devcontainer for this branch
/devcontainer myapp/main   # Target specific repo/branch
/devcontainer              # Show current status
/devcontainer off          # Disable, run commands on host
```

When a devcontainer is targeted:

- Most commands run inside the container automatically
- Git operations and file reading run on host
- Prefix with `HOST:` to force host execution

### Worktrees (Lightweight Filesystem Isolation)

> OpenCode V1 only — V2 supports worktrees natively; the `/worktree` and
> `/workspaces` commands are not registered under V2.

```
/worktree feature-x        # Create/target a worktree for this branch
/worktree myapp/main       # Target specific repo/branch
/worktree                  # Show current status
/worktree off              # Disable, run commands in original directory
```

When a worktree is targeted:

- Bash commands run in the worktree directory
- Same `HOST:` prefix for escaping
- Gitignored files are automatically copied from main repo

### Workspace Management

```
/workspaces                # List all workspaces (clones + worktrees)
/workspaces cleanup        # Find stale workspaces (not used in 7+ days)
```

## When to Use What

| Use Case                          | Recommendation  |
| --------------------------------- | --------------- |
| Project has devcontainer.json     | `/devcontainer` |
| Different dependencies per branch | `/devcontainer` |
| Quick branch work, same deps      | `/worktree`     |
| No Docker or Podman available     | `/worktree`     |
| Testing migrations/databases      | `/devcontainer` |

## Configuration

`~/.config/opencode/devcontainers/config.json`:

```json
{
  "portRangeStart": 13000,
  "portRangeEnd": 13099,
  "dockerPath": "podman",
  "dockerComposePath": "podman-compose"
}
```

`dockerPath` and `dockerComposePath` are optional. When unset, the plugin uses Docker when available, otherwise Podman. A Podman runtime requires either `podman-compose` or `docker-compose`; the plugin detects one automatically and reports an unsupported configuration when neither is available. Set both paths explicitly to use nonstandard executable locations.

## How It Works

### Devcontainers

1. Creates clone in `~/.local/share/opencode/clone/<repo>/<branch>/`
2. Copies gitignored secrets from main repo
3. Generates ephemeral override config with unique port
4. Starts container via `devcontainer up`

### Worktrees

1. Creates worktree in `~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/<repo>/<branch>/`
2. Copies gitignored secrets from main repo
3. Runs `direnv allow` if .envrc exists
4. Sets bash workdir to the worktree path

### Port/Database Isolation (Worktrees)

For worktrees, you can configure your `.envrc` to derive PORT and database settings from the worktree name to avoid conflicts:

```bash
# .envrc
export BRANCH_NAME=$(basename $(pwd))
export PORT=$((3000 + $(echo "$BRANCH_NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 1000))
export DATABASE_URL="postgres://localhost/${BRANCH_NAME//-/_}_development"
```

## Integration with opencode-pilot

When using [opencode-pilot](https://github.com/athal7/opencode-pilot) for automated issue processing, configure your `repos.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  myorg/myrepo:
    session:
      prompt_template: |
        /devcontainer issue-{number}

        {title}

        {body}
```

This starts an isolated devcontainer for each issue automatically.

## Known Issues

### OpenCode Desktop shows changes from wrong directory

When switching workspaces with `/devcontainer` or `/worktree`, OpenCode's internal directory context doesn't update. The "Session changes" panel continues showing diffs from the original directory.

**Workaround**: Start OpenCode directly in the target directory, or use separate terminal sessions per workspace.

**Upstream issue**: [anomalyco/opencode#6697](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/6697)

## Environment Variables

Override default paths:

- `OCDC_CONFIG_DIR` - Config directory (default: `~/.config/opencode/devcontainers`)
- `OCDC_CACHE_DIR` - Cache directory (default: `~/.cache/opencode-devcontainers`)
- `OCDC_CLONES_DIR` - Clones directory (default: `~/.local/share/opencode/clone`)
- `OCDC_WORKTREES_DIR` - Worktrees directory (default: `~/.local/share/opencode/worktree`)
- `OCDC_SESSIONS_DIR` - Sessions directory (default: `<cache>/opencode-sessions`)

## Related

- [opencode-pilot](https://github.com/athal7/opencode-pilot) - Automation layer for OpenCode (notifications, mobile UI, polling)

release workflow. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

# Contributing to opencode-devcontainers

Thanks for your interest in contributing!

## Development Setup

1. Clone the repository:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/timlaing/opencode-devcontainers.git
   cd opencode-devcontainers
   ```

2. Install dependencies:

   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

3. Install the devcontainer CLI (required for devcontainer operations):

   ```bash
   npm install -g @devcontainers/cli
   ```

4. Set up the plugin for local testing:
   ```bash
   # Add the repo to your opencode.json(c) — the repo root loads as a package
   # V2: "plugins": ["/path/to/opencode-devcontainers"]
   # V1: "plugin": ["/path/to/opencode-devcontainers"]
   ```

## Running the documentation site

Preview the MkDocs site locally:

```bash
pip install mkdocs-material
mkdocs serve   # http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

## Running Tests

Run the full test suite:

```bash
npm test
```

Run tests in watch mode:

```bash
npm run test:watch
```

Run tests with coverage (for local analysis; the `SonarQube` workflow computes
its own coverage in CI):

```bash
npm run test:coverage
```

Run the end-to-end check against a real OpenCode V2 runtime (requires the
`opencode` V2 CLI on PATH):

```bash
npm run e2e:v2
```

This loads the plugin through OpenCode's actual V2 plugin loader in a
sandboxed environment and exercises registration, `/devcontainer` command
execution, real agent-loop tool dispatch, the shell-interception hook,
multi-session routing, and stale-session cleanup over the HTTP API. It is
deterministic, offline, and free: only external dependencies (the LLM and
the container CLIs) are faked. Set `OCDC_E2E_KEEP=1` to keep the sandbox
directory for inspection.

## Writing Tests

Tests use Node.js built-in test runner. Example:

```javascript
import { describe, test, beforeEach, afterEach } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert";

describe("myFeature", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    // Setup
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    // Cleanup
  });

  test("does something", () => {
    assert.strictEqual(actual, expected);
  });
});
```

## Code Style

- Use ES modules (`import`/`export`)
- Use async/await for async operations
- Handle errors explicitly
- Add JSDoc comments for public functions

## Submitting Changes

1. Create a feature branch: `git checkout -b my-feature`
2. Make your changes
3. Run tests: `npm test`
4. Commit with conventional commit message:
   - `feat:` for new features
   - `fix:` for bug fixes
   - `docs:` for documentation
   - `refactor:` for refactoring
   - `test:` for tests
   - `chore:` for maintenance
5. Push and open a pull request

Pull request titles must also use Conventional Commits; the
`conventional pull request title` workflow rejects anything else.

## Labels and triage

Issue forms set `bug` or `enhancement` and `needs-triage`. Automation adds a
component label from the bug form. Maintainers remove `needs-triage` after
review and can adjust labels manually. PRs receive labels from changed paths,
conventional title prefixes (`fix:`, `feat:`, `docs:`, `ci:`, `test:`, `build:`),
and Dependabot authorship. Automatic labels are additive and preserve manual
labels. The labels are defined in the repository's
[Labels settings](https://github.com/timlaing/opencode-devcontainers/labels).

## Stale issues and pull requests

The stale workflow marks issues with no activity for 60 days and pull requests
with no activity for 30 days, then closes them after a further 14 days. Draft
PRs, items with milestones, and items labeled `keep-open`, `security`, or
`priority: high` are exempt.

## Dependency updates

Dependabot opens weekly grouped PRs for GitHub Actions and npm dependencies.
CI runs `npm audit --omit=dev` on every pull request as the `npm dependency
vulnerabilities` check. The check covers runtime dependencies only.

## SonarQube analysis

The `SonarQube` workflow runs alongside `CI` on main pushes and pull requests.
It installs the toolchain, runs the tests with coverage itself, then scans and
waits for the quality gate. It fails if the `SONAR_TOKEN` secret is missing.
`sonar-project.properties` documents the same source/test layout for local
analysis.

Project: `timlaing_opencode-devcontainers`, organization: `timlaing`, service:
`https://sonarcloud.io`. Supply Actions secret `SONAR_TOKEN` only after the Sonar
project exists with matching visibility. Disable Sonar automatic analysis when
using this CI workflow. The SonarQube badges in the README populate after the
first successful scan.

## Releasing

Releases are event-driven — publishing never happens on pushes to main:

1. Ensure `main` is green
2. `gh release create vX.Y.Z --target main --generate-notes`
3. The `Publish release` job in the `CI` workflow triggers on the release
   event, stamps the tag version, publishes to npmjs via trusted publishing
   (OIDC with provenance), and mirrors the same version to GitHub Packages
4. Re-running the job is safe — both publishes skip versions that already
   exist

# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

This repository and its issues are public. Do not put vulnerability details,
credentials, private keys, personal data or sensitive deployment information in
public issues, pull requests or discussions.

Report vulnerabilities privately through [GitHub private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/timlaing/opencode-devcontainers/security/advisories/new).
This route is available to first-time reporters and sends the report privately to
repository maintainers. Do not use a public issue as a substitute.

No response-time guarantee or older-release support commitment is offered.
Security fixes target the current development branch and the latest releases;
upgrade when a fix is published.

## Plugin boundaries

The plugin creates git clones and worktrees under `~/.local/share/opencode`,
starts devcontainers, allocates ports from a configurable range, and copies
gitignored files (such as `.env`) from your main repository into each workspace.
Treat those directories as sensitive as the original repository, and review what
your `.gitignore` marks as secret before enabling automatic copying. Commands
prefixed with `HOST:` execute on the host rather than inside the container; the
plugin does not sandbox the host from such commands.

Dependency audits and updates complement review; passing audits are not a claim
that the code has no vulnerabilities.

## Change

Describe the problem and the resulting behavior. Link related issues.

## Validation

List the commands/checks run and their results. Relevant checks include:

- `npm test` from the repository root.
- An actual OpenCode load/status check for entrypoint, hook or command changes.
- A devcontainer or worktree round trip for workspace lifecycle changes.

## Compatibility and configuration

Describe any changed options, migration steps or documented behavior. Write “None” if there are no changes.

- [ ] README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and `plugin/command/*.md` are updated where behavior changed.
- [ ] The change contains no live configuration, credentials, private keys or sensitive diagnostic data.

# Configuration

## Config file

`~/.config/opencode/devcontainers/config.json`:

```json
{
  "portRangeStart": 13000,
  "portRangeEnd": 13099,
  "dockerPath": "podman",
  "dockerComposePath": "podman-compose"
}
```

| Key                 | Default | Description                             |
| ------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `portRangeStart`    | `13000` | First port of the auto-allocation range |
| `portRangeEnd`      | `13099` | Last port of the auto-allocation range  |
| `dockerPath`        | auto    | Container runtime executable            |
| `dockerComposePath` | auto    | Compose executable                      |

`dockerPath` and `dockerComposePath` are optional. When unset, the plugin uses
Docker when available, otherwise Podman. A Podman runtime requires either
`podman-compose` or `docker-compose`; the plugin detects one automatically and
reports an unsupported configuration when neither is available. Set both paths
explicitly to use nonstandard executable locations.

## Tool permissions (V2)

The V2 `devcontainer` tool declares the permission key `devcontainer`, so you
can require explicit approval before it runs — including remove operations —
through OpenCode's permission configuration:

```json
{
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "devcontainer", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }
  ]
}
```

The remove flow always shows its warnings (uncommitted changes, other active
sessions) before doing anything, but those confirmations happen in the chat
and are enforced by the model. Gating the tool itself with a permission is the
independently enforced option if you want a user-approval step that the model
cannot skip.

## Environment variables

Override the default locations (mainly useful for testing or unusual setups):

| Variable             | Default                            |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `OCDC_CONFIG_DIR`    | `~/.config/opencode/devcontainers` |
| `OCDC_CACHE_DIR`     | `~/.cache/opencode-devcontainers`  |
| `OCDC_CLONES_DIR`    | `~/.local/share/opencode/clone`    |
| `OCDC_WORKTREES_DIR` | `~/.local/share/opencode/worktree` |
| `OCDC_SESSIONS_DIR`  | `<cache>/opencode-sessions`        |

## On-disk layout

| Path                        | Contents                                                  |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |

## Running the tests

```sh
npm ci
npm test               # full suite
npm run test:watch     # watch mode
npm run test:coverage  # coverage report (lcov in coverage/)
npm run e2e:v2         # end-to-end check against a real V2 runtime
```

The suites are hermetic: external commands (`devcontainer`, `docker`) are
replaced with fake executables placed on `PATH`, and every stateful directory
is redirected via `OCDC_*` environment variables into a per-test temp
directory. The shared harness lives in `test/unit/harness.js`.

- `test/unit/plugin.test.js` — the V1 implementation (`server()`): factory,
  all four tools, and the `tool.execute.before` hook
- `test/unit/plugin-v2.test.js` — the V2 implementation (`setup()`): the fake
  plugin context's registrations (command, tools, hook), the executors, and
  the shell interception hook
- `test/unit/core.*.test.js` — the core modules

CI also verifies that the combined entrypoint imports cleanly and exposes the
exact shape OpenCode's V2 loader requires (default export with `id` + `setup`)
alongside the V1 `server()` entrypoint. Loading in a live OpenCode V2 runtime
was validated against OpenCode 2.0.30 (`opencode plugin list` reports the
plugin's ID); note that `opencode plugin list` on a fresh machine does not
list project-scoped plugins, which is why CI asserts the entrypoint contract
directly instead of driving the CLI.

## End-to-end check (V2)

`scripts/e2e-v2.mjs` loads the plugin through OpenCode's real V2 plugin
loader and drives it over the HTTP API of a sandboxed `opencode serve`
instance, asserting the behaviors the unit tests' fake context cannot:

- plugin registration (state `active`) and the `/devcontainer` command in
  the real command registry
- `POST /session/{id}/command` execution: `$ARGUMENTS` substitution and
  `ctx.session.prompt` forwarding
- real agent-loop tool dispatch (`devcontainer`, `devcontainer_exec`) and
  background container start (clone + shimmed `devcontainer up`)
- the `execute.before` shell hook rewriting `npm test` into
  `devcontainer exec ...` (asserted on the tool result, which only the
  wrapped command can produce)
- multi-session routing (an unbound session runs on the host, with no
  leaked session state)
- stale-session cleanup at init against the real session store, including
  preservation of active sessions across a server restart

Only external dependencies are faked: a scripted OpenAI-compatible server
plays the model (canned tool calls, so the check is deterministic, offline,
and free), and `devcontainer`/`docker` are PATH shims. Every OpenCode
process runs with a sandboxed `HOME` and `OCDC_*` state directories; the
script never touches your real OpenCode service or providers.

## Releasing

Releases are event-driven, not commit-driven: publishing runs only when a
GitHub Release is published, never on pushes to `main`.

- Cut a release from a green `main`:

  ```sh
  gh release create vX.Y.Z --target main --generate-notes
  ```

- The `Publish release` job in the `CI` workflow stamps the tag version,
  publishes to npmjs with trusted publishing (OIDC + provenance — no
  long-lived npm tokens), and mirrors the same version to GitHub Packages
- Draft and prerelease releases are ignored; stable `vX.Y.Z` is the channel
- Re-running the publish job is safe: each registry skips a version that is
  already published

# opencode-devcontainers

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin for isolated branch workspaces using
devcontainers. Point a session at a branch and the plugin clones the repo,
builds and starts a devcontainer for it, and transparently routes the agent's
shell commands into that container.

!!! info "Community project"
    This is a community project and is not built by or affiliated with the
    OpenCode team.

## What it does

When you target a branch with `/devcontainer`, the plugin:

- **Clones** the repo into a per-branch workspace (gitignored secrets such as
  `.env` are copied from your main checkout)
- **Builds and starts** a devcontainer via the
  [`devcontainers/cli`](https://github.com/devcontainers/cli)
- **Allocates a unique port** from a configurable range (default 13000–13099)
  through an ephemeral override config, so parallel workspaces don't collide
- **Routes commands into the container**: once a devcontainer is targeted,
  shell commands run inside it automatically — with a `HOST:` escape hatch and
  automatic host execution for git and file-reading commands
- **Tracks session state**, so the agent remembers which container each session
  is targeting, and cleans up stale sessions and finished startup jobs

## OpenCode V1 and V2 support

One package supports both plugin APIs:

| OpenCode version | Plugin API            | Devcontainers                      | Worktrees                                  |
| ---------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| V2 (2.x)         | V2 (`plugins` config) | ✅                                 | Native — use OpenCode's built-in worktrees |
| V1 ≥ 1.18.29     | V1 (`plugin` config)  | ✅                                 | ✅ `/worktree`, `/workspaces`              |
| V1 < 1.18.29     | V1                    | pin `opencode-devcontainers@0.5.1` | pin `opencode-devcontainers@0.5.1`         |

V2 registers only the devcontainer functionality, because OpenCode V2 supports
worktrees natively (`/worktree_create` and friends). See
[Migrating to OpenCode V2](migration.md) for details.

## Quick start

```jsonc
// OpenCode V2 — opencode.json(c)
{
  "plugins": ["@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"],
}
```

```jsonc
// OpenCode V1 (≥ 1.18.29) — ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
{
  "plugin": ["@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"],
}
```

Then in a session, from inside your git repository:

```
/devcontainer feature-x
```

Full instructions on the [Installation](installation.md) page.

## Requirements

- Docker (or Podman) available to the `devcontainer` CLI
- The devcontainer CLI: `npm install -g @devcontainers/cli`
- A `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` (or `devcontainer.json`) in the target
  repository

# Installation

The package is published to **both** registries as
`@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers`:

- **npmjs** (recommended) —
  [`@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers).
  Public reads need no token, so this is the default for most setups.
- **GitHub Packages** —
  [packages](https://github.com/timlaing/opencode-devcontainers/packages).
  Requires a token for every operation, even reads. Useful if your scope is
  already mapped to `npm.pkg.github.com`, or as a fallback.

OpenCode installs npm plugins automatically when they appear in your
configuration. Because both registries use the `@timlaing` scope, a
`.npmrc` scope mapping decides which one resolves — see
[Registry setup](#registry-setup).

## Registry setup

npm/bun resolve the `@timlaing` scope through whatever the scope is mapped
to in `.npmrc`. Do **one** of the following — per project (next to where you
run OpenCode) or globally in `~/.npmrc`:

**npmjs (recommended, no token):**

```ini
@timlaing:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
```

**GitHub Packages (token required for reads):**

```ini
@timlaing:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}
```

then export a token with the `read:packages` scope (a classic PAT —
GitHub's npm registry does not accept fine-grained tokens):

```sh
export NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=github_pat_...
```

If your OpenCode install uses a package manager that ignores `.npmrc`
scope mappings, install the plugin from git instead — no registry auth
needed. OpenCode V1 reads the **singular** `plugin` key:

```jsonc
{
  "plugin": ["github:timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"],
}
```

## OpenCode V2

Add the plugin to `opencode.json(c)` — globally
(`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`) or per project:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"],
}
```

You can pin a version with `@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers@1.2.3`, or pass
options with the object form:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [{ "package": "@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers", "options": {} }],
}
```

If your package manager ignores `.npmrc` scope mappings, install from git
instead — V2 reads the plural `plugins` key:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": ["github:timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"],
}
```

Verify the plugin loads:

```sh
opencode plugin list
```

`opencode-devcontainers` should appear with its version. This lists
user-scoped plugins; on a fresh machine it does not list project-scoped
plugins. If you installed the plugin per project, verify it from inside an
OpenCode session instead — the `/devcontainer` command should be available.

## OpenCode V1 (≥ 1.18.29)

Add to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugin": ["@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"],
}
```

## OpenCode V1 (< 1.18.29)

Older V1 releases predate the combined V1/V2 entrypoint. Pin the last
V1-only release:

```jsonc
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-devcontainers@0.5.1"],
}
```

!!! note "Package rename"
`opencode-devcontainers@0.5.1` and earlier were published on npmjs under
the unscoped name by the original author (that registry needs no scope
mapping). This fork publishes the `@timlaing`-scoped package on npmjs
(canonical) and mirrors it to GitHub Packages.

## Dependencies

- **devcontainer CLI** — required for the devcontainer functionality:

  ```sh
  npm install -g @devcontainers/cli
  ```

- **Docker or Podman** — the container runtime used by the devcontainer CLI.
  The plugin auto-detects either; see
  [Configuration](configuration.md) to pin specific executables.

- **git** — used to clone repositories into workspaces.

# Migrating to OpenCode V2

This page covers what changes when you move an existing setup to OpenCode V2,
and answers the questions from
[issue #1](https://github.com/timlaing/opencode-devcontainers/issues/1).

## TL;DR

1. Update the config key and restart OpenCode:

   ```jsonc
   // V1
   { "plugin": ["@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"] }

   // V2
   { "plugins": ["@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers"] }
   ```

2. Keep using `/devcontainer` exactly as before.
3. If you used `/worktree` or `/workspaces`, switch to OpenCode V2's native
   worktree support.

## What changed and why

OpenCode V2 introduced a new plugin API. V1 plugin _implementations_ do not run
in V2 at all — this package therefore ships a combined entrypoint that exposes
both APIs from one default export:

- **V2** loads the `Plugin.define({ id, setup })` definition and registers the
  devcontainer tools, the `/devcontainer` command, and the shell interception
  hook through `ctx.tool.transform`, `ctx.command.transform`, and
  `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before")`.
- **V1 (≥ 1.18.29)** calls `server()` and registers the full V1 tool set, as
  before.

Internally both entrypoints share the same handler core
(`plugin/handlers.js` and `plugin/core/`), so behavior is identical across
versions and covered by one test suite.

### Devcontainers: unchanged behavior

Everything about the devcontainer workflow is preserved:

- Branch targeting, background startup, and the "still starting" feedback
- Port allocation and ephemeral override configs
- Session isolation (each session remembers its own container)
- Command routing with automatic host execution for git/file commands
- The `HOST:` escape prefix
- `/devcontainer rm` and workspace cleanup

### Worktrees: use the native V2 support

OpenCode V2 has first-class worktrees: a `worktree` configuration key,
`worktree_create` / `worktree_list` / `worktree_remove` utilities, a
`ctx.worktree` plugin API, and inventory tracking per project. Because of that,
**this plugin does not register its V1 worktree tooling under V2** — the V2
plugin exposes only the devcontainer functionality.

To migrate a worktree workflow:

```sh
# V1
/worktree feature-x

# V2 equivalent — native support
# (create the worktree, then move the session into it)
```

V2-native worktrees also handle the "workdir" routing that the V1 plugin's
`/worktree` mode implemented, so no interception hook is needed for them.

### Command files → command registration

Under V1 the plugin copied command files (`devcontainer.md`, …) into your
config directory. Under V2 it registers the `/devcontainer` command directly
via the plugin API — nothing is written to your config directory, and stale
copies of the old command files are no longer installed.

If you used the V1 plugin before upgrading, delete the command files it
installed so the obsolete `/worktree` and `/workspaces` commands (and a
duplicate `/devcontainer`) do not linger as user commands in V2:

```sh
rm -f ~/.config/opencode/command/devcontainer.md \
      ~/.config/opencode/command/worktree.md \
      ~/.config/opencode/command/workspaces.md
```

Only remove these files if they came from the plugin — if you authored your
own commands with these names, keep them.

## Support policy

| OpenCode     | Supported package version                   | Notes                                      |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| V2 (2.x)     | `@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers` (latest) | Devcontainers only; worktrees are native   |
| V1 ≥ 1.18.29 | `@timlaing/opencode-devcontainers` (latest) | Full V1 feature set                        |
| V1 < 1.18.29 | `opencode-devcontainers@0.5.1`              | Last release of the archived upstream line |

V1 support is provided by the same package and is tested by the same suite;
there are no plans to drop it while the `server()` entrypoint remains
supported by V1. The V1 code path will be removed only if a future OpenCode
release removes V1 plugin loading entirely.

## Migrating state from V1

Session files and workspace state live under `~/.cache/opencode-devcontainers`
and are format-compatible — no migration is needed. Stale session files are
cleaned up automatically at startup, exactly as under V1.

If you previously ran the unscoped `opencode-devcontainers` package, remove the
old config entry before adding the scoped one so both are not loaded:

```sh
opencode plugin remove opencode-devcontainers
opencode plugin add @timlaing/opencode-devcontainers
```

# Usage

## Targeting a devcontainer

```
/devcontainer feature-x    # Start/target a devcontainer for this branch
/devcontainer myapp/main   # Target a specific repo/branch
/devcontainer              # Show current status
/devcontainer off          # Disable — run commands on the host
/devcontainer rm <branch>  # Remove a devcontainer workspace
/devcontainer rm all       # Remove all devcontainer workspaces
```

The first time you target a branch, the plugin:

1. Clones the repository into `~/.local/share/opencode/clone/<repo>/<branch>/`
2. Copies gitignored secrets (`.env`, credentials, etc.) from the main repo
3. Generates an ephemeral override config with a unique forwarded port
4. Starts the container with `devcontainer up` **in the background**

Because builds can take minutes, the session is marked as _starting_: the agent
gets a friendly "container is still starting" response instead of a cryptic
failure until the job completes.

## How command routing works

Once a devcontainer is targeted for the session, shell commands are wrapped in
`devcontainer exec --workspace-folder <workspace> -- <command>` and therefore
run inside the container.

Three things run on the **host** instead:

- **Git and file commands** (`git`, `gh`, `cat`, `grep`, `ls`, …) — the repo
  is mounted into the container, and running these on the host keeps snapshots
  and diffs accurate
- **Explicit escapes** — prefix any command with `HOST:` to force host
  execution:

  ```
  HOST: docker ps
  ```

- **Commands with a foreign working directory** — if the agent sets a workdir
  outside the targeted workspace, the command is left untouched

`/devcontainer off` (or a session with no target) returns everything to normal.

## The tools

The slash command is sugar over two tools the agent can also call directly:

| Tool                | Purpose                                                           |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `devcontainer`      | Target, inspect, disable, or remove devcontainers for the session |
| `devcontainer_exec` | Execute a command inside the session's devcontainer               |

## Worktrees (OpenCode V1 only)

!!! note "V2 users"
    OpenCode V2 supports worktrees natively — use the built-in
    `worktree_create` / `worktree_list` / `worktree_remove` utilities and the
    `worktree` configuration instead of this plugin. The `/worktree` and
    `/workspaces` commands only exist in the V1 plugin API.

```
/worktree feature-x        # Create/target a worktree for this branch
/worktree myapp/main       # Target a specific repo/branch
/worktree                  # Show current status
/worktree off              # Disable — run commands in the original directory
```

Worktrees provide lightweight filesystem isolation: bash commands run in the
worktree directory, and gitignored files are copied from the main repo.

### Port/database isolation with worktrees

Configure your `.envrc` to derive `PORT` and database settings from the
worktree name to avoid conflicts:

```bash
# .envrc
export BRANCH_NAME=$(basename $(pwd))
export PORT=$((3000 + $(echo "$BRANCH_NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 1000))
export DATABASE_URL="postgres://localhost/${BRANCH_NAME//-/_}_development"
```

## Workspace management (OpenCode V1 only)

```
/workspaces                # List all workspaces (clones + worktrees)
/workspaces cleanup        # Find stale workspaces (not used in 7+ days)
```

## When to use what

| Use case                             | Recommendation                            |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| Project has a devcontainer.json      | `/devcontainer`                           |
| Different dependencies per branch    | `/devcontainer`                           |
| Testing migrations/databases         | `/devcontainer`                           |
| Quick branch work, same dependencies | `/worktree` (V1) or native worktrees (V2) |
| No Docker or Podman available        | `/worktree` (V1) or native worktrees (V2) |

## Automation

When using [opencode-pilot](https://github.com/athal7/opencode-pilot) for
automated issue processing, configure your `repos.yaml` to start an isolated
devcontainer per issue:

```yaml
repos:
  myorg/myrepo:
    session:
      prompt_template: |
        /devcontainer issue-{number}

        {title}

        {body}
```

## Known issues

**OpenCode Desktop shows changes from the wrong directory.** When switching
workspaces with `/devcontainer`, OpenCode's internal directory context doesn't
update — the "Session changes" panel keeps showing diffs from the original
directory. Workaround: start OpenCode directly in the target directory, or use
separate terminal sessions per workspace.
([anomalyco/opencode#6697](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/6697))

---
description: Target a devcontainer - /devcontainer <branch>, off. Or remove: /devcontainer rm <branch>, or rm all
---

Call the `devcontainer` tool with `target` set to: $ARGUMENTS

If no arguments provided, call `devcontainer` with no target to show current status.

If a `rm` command returns a message asking for confirmation, ask the user if they want to proceed. If they agree, call the tool again with the same arguments plus `confirmed: true`.

---
description: Manage workspaces - /workspaces [cleanup]
---

Call the `workspaces` tool with action set to: $ARGUMENTS

If no arguments provided, list all workspaces with status.
If 'cleanup' provided, identify stale workspaces for removal.

---
description: Target a git worktree - /worktree <branch> or off
---

Call the `worktree` tool with:
- `target`: $ARGUMENTS
- `workdir`: the current working directory (use the directory you are working in)

If no arguments provided, call `worktree` with no target to show current status.

Example: `worktree(target: "feature-branch", workdir: "/path/to/repo")`
